page.layout: One printed page of text in a single column, with the chapter number and title centred above it. Show-through from the reverse side runs along the left edge and is omitted. The catchword "XVI. DE" stands at the foot, right.

main_text.head: XV. DE STATV EPIRI.
main_text.p: PIRRUS quondam etiam sub regibus suis non vili parte libertatis gavisa fuit. Nam ut prodit Plutarchus in Pyrrho, rex & populus quotannis solenni in conventu in regione Moloffidis mutuo juramento obstringere se solebant, ille secundum leges se regnaturum, hic regnum se ei conservaturos regnanti secundum leges. Eadem vero Epirus à Pyrrhi abnepte Deidamiâ, cum ipsa careret liberis, integrâ & plenâ libertate donata suam quoque rempublicam peculiarem habuit per tempora illa ea- rum : sed quae forma ejus fuerit, hacte-[?]is me latet. Hoc tantum apud Polybium reperio, tres eodem tempore praesides eam habuisse, qui rempublicam gererent : an plures etiam fuerint, non constat. Retinuit autem Epirus quacunque libertatem à Macedonibus pe concussam ad casum usq; Achaeo-rum. Quo tempore ipsa quoque provinciae Achaiae attributa est.

page.notes: The first line of the drop cap reads "PIRRVS" with a decorated P; transcribed as PIRRUS, with u for the vowel. Several lines are damaged or show through from the reverse, notably "peculiarem" (only "liarem" clearly legible at the line start, reconstructed as "culiarem"), "ea-rum" (partly obscured), and the line ending "hacte-" followed by "is" (the continuation is uncertain). Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout, including "suam", "sed", "est" and "usq;". The word "concussam" is set with the ss ligature, which looks like "ff". The text "pe concussam" may contain a damaged letter before "concussam". Marginal show-through and stains are not transcribed.
